pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is low on a net basis, and the pro forma figures do not change that. Net debt at September 30, 2026 was USD 319 million, or 0.37x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 867 million; pro forma for the October 30, 2026 redemption of the 2030 notes it is USD 321 million and 0.37x, and pro forma for the December 3, 2026 dividend payment it is USD 338.93 million and 0.39x. Gross debt of USD 1,480 million is 1.71x, up from 1.28x at FY2024 because EBITDA fell by more than debt did; on the company's adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,001 million the net and gross figures are 0.32x and 1.48x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

Earnings are the weakest dimension and carry the downside. Last-twelve-months reported EBITDA is 32.32% below FY2024 and adjusted EBITDA 27.57% below, on revenue 14.95% lower at USD 4,689 million. The Middle East, North Africa and Asia region, 40.26% of revenue, fell by USD 191 million over nine months because of the Iran conflict, and Well Construction and Completions margin fell to 23.91% from 27.18%, while Production and Intervention margin rose to 21.27%. No backlog or contract duration is disclosed, so revenue visibility beyond the company's expectation of an improving fourth quarter is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

Cash flow quality improved in 2026 but is helped by receivable collections. Free cash flow after capital expenditures was USD 362 million over nine months against USD 233 million, which is 50.99% of adjusted EBITDA against 30.03%, and capital expenditures were 4.15% of revenue, inside the company's 3% to 5% range. USD 186 million of operating cash flow came from receivable collections, so the figure overstates the repeatable level; against that, factoring proceeds fell by USD 215 million, so the cash flow does not rest on selling receivables. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

Liquidity covers every scheduled obligation, with two qualifications. Cash of USD 1,161 million (pro forma cash after the redemption is not established), of which USD 164 million cannot be immediately repatriated, plus USD 599 million of the undrawn facility that can be borrowed, gives USD 1,760 million against gross debt of USD 1,480 million, or 1.19x; USD 167 million of the facility is for performance letters of credit only, and USD 531 million of letters of credit and USD 534 million of surety bonds could be called. Covenant levels are stated, but their definitions and the company's calculated ratios are not, so covenant headroom is not established here. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C26; calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C34; calculation C45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

Refinancing risk is low because the maturity wall is distant and shrinking. The 2033 notes carry USD 1,200 million of principal, the credit agreement runs to September 18, 2030 once the 2030 notes are gone, and the annual report schedules only USD 29 million of maturities in 2026, USD 20 million in 2027, USD 9 million in 2028 and USD 4 million in 2029, all finance leases. Redeeming USD 236 million of 2030 notes from cash saves about USD 20 million of annual cash interest; no filing yet confirms completion. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-20_a2026-q3ex991earningsrelea.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86

Governance and financial policy add little risk on the evidence available. Business & governance names no sponsor or controlling holder and rates sponsor and governance risk low on documented behaviour; shareholder returns of USD 113 million are 31.22% of nine-month free cash flow, and the 2025 refinancing and the planned redemption reduce debt. The open questions are the intellectual property transition inside the move to Delaware and three changes of note obligors since 2022, which cannot be tested without the indentures. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C38; calculation C47; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

Customer and country concentration is the second-order risk. The largest Mexican customer is 14% of net receivables and has a record of late payment, and Russia is 9% of revenue and holds USD 128 million of cash. At these levels they are collection and trapped-cash risks and not solvency risks, but they sit in the same regions as the disruption that is lowering earnings. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C41; calculation C42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

The outlook is for gradual recovery with the Middle East timing uncertain. The company expects activity to improve through the rest of 2026 in North America and Latin America and from the NCS acquisition, and a meaningful fourth-quarter ramp in adjusted EBITDA, and it calls the pace of Middle East recovery the main uncertainty. For scale, a fourth quarter at the fourth-quarter 2025 level of USD 291 million would be 14.57% above the third quarter's USD 254 million; WTI averaged USD 84.98 over nine months against USD 67.40 a year earlier, a price rise that has not lifted Middle East activity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; EX-99.1_2026-10-20_a2026-q3ex991earningsrelea.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C39; calculation C40

runs.text: Strengths. Net debt is small against earnings: net debt of USD 319 million (USD 321 million pro forma) is 0.37x last-twelve-months EBITDA (0.37x pro forma), so a further decline in EBITDA would raise leverage but not threaten the debt service capacity of a group that holds USD 1,161 million of cash (pro forma cash not established). The company controls its largest discretionary uses of cash: capital expenditures are 4.15% of revenue against a guided range of 3% to 5%, and USD 246 million of buyback authorisation can be left unused, which gives a means to protect cash in a downturn. The business spans three segments and four regions, and Production and Intervention margin rose to 21.27% while Well Construction and Completions fell, so the weakness is not uniform. The debt profile has no bond maturity before 2033 once the 2030 notes are redeemed, and the company is retiring them from cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; calculation C26; calculation C23; calculation C19; calculation C18; calculation C36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38

Weaknesses. Earnings fell by about a third from FY2024 because a region that supplies 40.26% of revenue was disrupted, and the company gives no backlog to show when earnings recover. Part of the 2026 cash flow is receivable collections of USD 186 million that will not repeat, so reported free cash flow is not a run-rate. The largest Mexican customer, 14% of net receivables, pays late, and USD 164 million of cash cannot be immediately repatriated. Ownership and legal documents were not supplied, so control rights, guarantor coverage and covenant headroom are unknown, and the planned move to Delaware carries an intellectual property transition whose creditor effect is undisclosed. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C17; calculation C24; calculation C41; calculation C32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

Business risk in credit terms. The industry has four large competitors and customers that are mostly national and international oil companies, so pricing and technology pressure come from both sides, and spending follows oil prices and rig counts. Political and trade developments matter directly: the Iran conflict has cut Middle East activity, Russia carries sanctions and nationalisation risk, and tariffs are described as a possible cost. Technology and the energy transition are a long-run factor for the products and the credit, but the filings give no evidence that either is a primary driver over the debt's life. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_wfrd-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wfrd-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: The NCS Multistage acquisition was agreed on May 31, 2026 and completed on September 1, 2026 for total consideration of USD 128 million, paid in shares, cash and assumed equity awards, and NCS is now a wholly owned subsidiary that adds completions technology and unconventional-market exposure. No new debt was issued in 2026 through the latest filing; the last issue was the USD 1,200 million of 2033 notes on October 6, 2025, which refinanced most of the 2030 notes, and on October 20, 2026 the company gave notice to redeem the remaining USD 236 million of the 2030 notes on October 30, 2026 from cash. The parent's redomestication from Ireland to Delaware, approved by shareholders on September 3, 2026, is expected in the fourth quarter and is not a financing transaction. fields.value: Net debt was USD 319 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 321 million pro forma for the planned October 30, 2026 redemption of the 2030 notes), or 0.37x last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 867 million, against USD 718 million at FY2024. Gross debt of USD 1,480 million is 1.71x, up from 1.28x, so the improvement came from cash build and repayment, not from earnings. Liquidity is ample, with USD 1,161 million of cash and USD 766 million undrawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is low on a net basis and has risen on a gross basis. Net debt fell by USD 399 million from FY2024 to USD 319 million, because cash rose by USD 245 million to USD 1,161 million and total debt fell by USD 154 million to USD 1,480 million. Against last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 867 million, net leverage is 0.37x and gross leverage 1.71x; on the company's adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,001 million they are 0.32x and 1.48x. Gross leverage was 1.28x at FY2024, so the credit has deleveraged through the numerator while the denominator shrank. The company's own net leverage of 0.28x also deducts USD 37 million of restricted cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are the weak side of the credit. Last-twelve-months EBITDA is 32.32% below FY2024 on the reported basis and 27.57% below on the company's adjusted basis, on revenue 14.95% lower at USD 4,689 million. The company attributes the decline mainly to Middle East disruption from the Iran conflict and to lower North America activity; Well Construction and Completions adjusted EBITDA fell by USD 54 million over nine months while Production and Intervention rose by USD 13 million. Third-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 254 million was 5.58% below a year earlier and 13.90% above the second quarter, and the company expects a meaningful fourth-quarter ramp that the filings do not quantify.

fields.value: Cash generation improved in 2026, but not all of the improvement is repeatable. Cash from operations was USD 503 million over nine months against USD 408 million, and free cash flow after capital expenditures rose to USD 362 million from USD 233 million as capital expenditures fell to USD 141 million from USD 175 million. Receivable collections supplied USD 186 million of the 2026 figure; without them, cash from operations would be USD 317 million, below the USD 386 million of the prior year on the same basis. Factoring proceeds fell by USD 215 million to USD 16 million, so the improvement does not rest on selling receivables.

fields.value: Liquidity is strong, but the headline overstates what is freely available. The USD 1,000 million credit agreement is undrawn, with USD 766 million of headroom after letters of credit, but only USD 599 million of that can be borrowed, because the annual report limits USD 400 million of the commitment to performance letters of credit and the quarterly reports do not restate the split. Letters of credit under bilateral lines of USD 297 million and surety bonds of USD 534 million could be called if contract obligations were breached.

fields.value: The maturity wall is distant and is about to shrink. The company gave notice on October 20, 2026 to redeem all USD 236 million of the 2030 notes on October 30, 2026 with cash, and no source yet confirms completion. That leaves the 2033 notes, USD 1,200 million of principal due in 2033, as the only bond; before then the annual report schedules only USD 29 million of maturities in 2026 and USD 20 million in 2027, mainly finance leases. The company says the redemption cuts annual cash interest by about USD 20 million, and it ends the clause that would pull the credit agreement's maturity forward while more than USD 200 million of the 2030 notes remain outstanding.

Fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA that fails to rise from the third quarter's USD 254 million, a further Middle East escalation, or slower collection from the largest Mexican customer would turn the view negative, because cash rather than earnings supports the net leverage. Adjusted EBITDA stabilising near USD 1,001 million with gross leverage below 1.48x would turn it positive.

The largest Mexican customer is 14% of net receivables and has a record of late payment, and Russia is 9% of revenue and holds USD 128 million of cash. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The outlook is for gradual recovery with the Middle East timing uncertain. The company expects activity to improve through the rest of 2026 in North America and Latin America and from the NCS acquisition, and a meaningful fourth-quarter ramp in adjusted EBITDA, and it calls the pace of Middle East recovery the main uncertainty. For scale, a fourth quarter at the fourth-quarter 2025 level of USD 291 million would be 14.57% above the third quarter's USD 254 million; WTI averaged USD 84.98 over nine months against USD 67.40 a year earlier, a price rise that has not lifted Middle East activity.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that net leverage has fallen to 0.37x (0.37x pro forma for the October 30, 2026 redemption), that nine-month free cash flow was USD 362 million, that each agency holds a positive outlook, and that management still expects a meaningful fourth-quarter recovery. A fourth quarter that fails to lift adjusted EBITDA above the third quarter's USD 254 million, a reversal of the USD 186 million of receivable collections, or a rise in the largest Mexican customer's 14% share of receivables would turn the view negative. Adjusted EBITDA holding near USD 1,001 million with free cash flow conversion near 50.99% would turn it positive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Net debt is small against earnings: net debt of USD 319 million (USD 321 million pro forma) is 0.37x last-twelve-months EBITDA (0.37x pro forma), so a further decline in EBITDA would raise leverage but not threaten the debt service capacity of a group that holds USD 1,161 million of cash (pro forma cash not established). The company controls its largest discretionary uses of cash: capital expenditures are 4.15% of revenue against a guided range of 3% to 5%, and USD 246 million of buyback authorisation can be left unused, which gives a means to protect cash in a downturn. The business spans three segments and four regions, and Production and Intervention margin rose to 21.27% while Well Construction and Completions fell, so the weakness is not uniform. The debt profile has no bond maturity before 2033 once the 2030 notes are redeemed, and the company is retiring them from cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Earnings fell by about a third from FY2024 because a region that supplies 40.26% of revenue was disrupted, and the company gives no backlog to show when earnings recover. Part of the 2026 cash flow is receivable collections of USD 186 million that will not repeat, so reported free cash flow is not a run-rate. The largest Mexican customer, 14% of net receivables, pays late, and USD 164 million of cash cannot be immediately repatriated. Ownership and legal documents were not supplied, so control rights, guarantor coverage and covenant headroom are unknown, and the planned move to Delaware carries an intellectual property transition whose creditor effect is undisclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk in credit terms. The industry has four large competitors and customers that are mostly national and international oil companies, so pricing and technology pressure come from both sides, and spending follows oil prices and rig counts. Political and trade developments matter directly: the Iran conflict has cut Middle East activity, Russia carries sanctions and nationalisation risk, and tariffs are described as a possible cost. Technology and the energy transition are a long-run factor for the products and the credit, but the filings give no evidence that either is a primary driver over the debt's life.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business sells services and equipment across the well life cycle, with services at 61.35% of nine-month revenue, so revenue follows customer drilling and workover activity and not long-term contracts, and the filings give no backlog. Cost of products and services is 69% of revenue, headcount reductions lowered personnel costs and restructuring charges fell to USD 28 million from USD 51 million, which shows some cost flexibility, so margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure but, as an analyst judgement, not under a deep fall in activity. Capital intensity is moderate, working capital is the main swing factor in cash flow, and the receivable position of a Mexican customer with a history of late payment is the observed pressure point.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the tailwinds are higher oil prices, higher worldwide rig counts, the NCS completions portfolio, the end of the 2030 notes' cash interest and, from 2027, the USD 20 million to USD 30 million of annual cash savings the company expects from the redomestication. The headwinds are the Middle East disruption, the new tariffs the company describes as a possible cost, the ongoing Russia exposure, and the cost of integrating NCS. Over three to five years the filings point to energy security and offshore and deepwater spending as structural supports, which is management language and is not evidenced by contract data in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario starts with the Middle East disruption continuing through 2027 while oil prices fall back from their 2026 level. The first operational break would be further declines in drilling-related, wireline, liner hanger and cementation activity in a region that supplies 40.26% of revenue, which pushes down segment EBITDA, as it already has in Well Construction and Completions. Cost of products and services is 69% of revenue, so EBITDA would fall faster than revenue unless headcount and supply costs are cut as quickly as activity falls. The financial transmission is lower operating cash flow, aggravated by a reversal of the receivable collections that supported 2026 and by slower payment from the largest Mexican customer, while dividends and buybacks continue unless the company pauses them. Liquidity would hold: cash of USD 1,161 million (pro forma cash not established) is 78.45% of gross debt, the facility adds USD 599 million, and the company has levers in capital expenditures, the buyback and factoring. Gross leverage would rise above 1.71x and net leverage above 0.37x, and the observable triggers are a fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA at or below USD 254 million, a growing share of receivables owed by the Mexican customer, cash that cannot be repatriated rising above USD 164 million, and any draw on the facility. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, but the covenant tests cannot be checked without the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Weatherford presents a diversified business profile supported by a small net debt of USD 319 million (USD 321 million pro forma), cash of USD 1,161 million (pro forma cash not established) and a distant maturity wall, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that have fallen about a third from FY2024 and by concentration in a disrupted region. Cash-flow durability is adequate and not strong, because USD 186 million of 2026 operating cash flow was receivable collections. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on an EBITDA recovery before the credit agreement matures in 2030 and on its legal terms, which were not supplied. The primary downside path is a prolonged Middle East disruption with collections reversing. Further analysis would require the indentures and credit agreement, the proxy statement, peer and market data, backlog, and the company's covenant calculations. Fundamental credit analysis is complete; top risk: earnings concentration in the Middle East.
